description: Three-panel composite of tensile-property line plots, all sharing a dual y-axis layout: left axis "Strength (MPa)", right axis "TE or δ (%)". Each panel plots four quantities: UTS (magenta squares), YS (blue diamonds), TE (black triangles) and δ (red crosses); solid curves correspond to water-quenched samples and dotted curves to water-quenched plus aged samples (aging at 550 °C for 24 h in air, solutionizing at 1100 °C for 2 h per the caption). (a) "Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl", x-axis "Al (wt%)" from 0 to 12: solid UTS starts just above the 800 MPa gridline, dips to a minimum near 2 wt% Al, stays roughly flat to 8 wt% and then climbs to near the 900 MPa gridline at 10-12 wt% Al; the dotted UTS begins far lower (near the 500 MPa gridline) and rises steeply above about 8 wt% Al to the top of the scale. YS rises from just above 300 MPa to above 700 MPa at 12 wt% Al. TE is highest at 0 wt% Al, falls at 2 wt%, and shows a peak near 10 wt% Al. δ (red crosses) is plotted only at about 10 and 12 wt% Al, near 5-10%. (b) "Fe-30Mn-0.4C-xAl", Al (wt%) 0-11: solid and dotted UTS fall from above the 800 MPa gridline to a minimum near 2 wt% Al then rise steeply to about 800 MPa at 11 wt% Al; YS mirrors this with a minimum near 250 MPa at 2 wt%; TE peaks at 2 wt% Al (~70%) and declines at higher Al, while δ rises monotonically from ~0 to about 60% between 2 and 11 wt% Al. (c) "Fe-30Mn-9Al-xC", the only panel with x-axis "C (wt%)" from 0 to 2 and a left axis extending to 1200 MPa: UTS rises from near the 800 MPa gridline to above 1000 MPa, YS from ~450 MPa to near 900 MPa, TE peaks near 0.75 wt% C (~70%) and δ falls from about 50% at 0.3 wt% C to near zero by 1 wt% C.

observations.observation: All three panels share the same axis convention: left y-axis labelled "Strength (MPa)" and right y-axis labelled "TE or δ (%)", with four curve families identified by symbol/colour (magenta squares = UTS, blue diamonds = YS, black triangles = TE, red crosses = δ).
Panel (a) is labelled "Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl" with x-axis "Al (wt%)" spanning 0 to 12; panel (b) is labelled "Fe-30Mn-0.4C-xAl" with x-axis "Al (wt%)" spanning 0 to 11.
Panel (c) is labelled "Fe-30Mn-9Al-xC" and is the only panel whose x-axis is "C (wt%)" (0 to 2) with the Strength axis extended to 1200 MPa.
In every panel the UTS curve lies above the YS curve, and the right-hand-axis curves (TE and δ) occupy the lower part of each plot.

In panel (a) the dotted (aged) UTS curve lies well below the solid (water-quenched) UTS curve for low Al contents (up to ~7 wt% Al) but crosses above it and rises steeply at higher Al, reaching the top of the plotted range at 11-12 wt% Al.
In panel (a) the δ (red cross) data points appear only at the two highest Al contents (about 10 and 12 wt% Al) and lie near 5-10%.
In panel (b) the δ curve rises monotonically with Al from about 2 wt% upward while TE falls, and the solid (quenched) and dotted (aged) curves nearly coincide.
In panel (c) both strength curves rise with increasing C while the δ curve falls steeply to near zero by about 1 wt% C.

The caption states the steels were solutionized at 1100 °C for 2 h, that solid curves are from water-quenched samples and dotted curves from water-quenched then aged samples (550 °C for 24 h in air), and that data are taken from Refs. [6,9,74,82,118].

The caption labels only panels (a) and (b) — as Fe-30Mn-1.2CxAl and Fe-30Mn-0.4C-xAl — and states the figure shows the effect of Al on microstructure and tensile properties; the third panel (c), Fe-30Mn-9Al-xC, is not described in the supplied caption.

The citing text refers to the second series as "Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl" steels (Fig. 27b), whereas the panel in the image is printed "Fe-30Mn-0.4C-xAl"; the caption also gives Fe-30Mn-0.4C-xAl, so the image and caption agree and the body text differs.

The citing text states that for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl series the solution-treated microstructure is single-phase austenite for 0-9% Al and δ-ferrite is introduced above 10% Al, which is consistent with the δ points appearing only at high Al in panel (a).
The citing text states that additions of less than 7% Al to Fe-30Mn-1.2C TWIP steel slightly increase YS but decrease UTS and TE, whereas above 8% Al, YS, UTS and TE all increase again.

The citing text states that aging at 550 °C greatly reduces UTS and TE of the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C steel, only weakly affects the 2-7% Al alloys, and produces strong age hardening only above 8% Al (attributed to κ-carbide precipitation).

The citing text states that in the 0.4C series the strength increase with Al is due to solution hardening of Al in ferrite (40 MPa/wt% Al) being stronger than in austenite (10 MPa/wt% Al), and that the ductility drop is due to increasing ferrite and suppressed twinning.

subfigures.description: Tensile properties of Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl versus Al (wt%) from 0 to 12; dual y-axis (Strength MPa left, TE or δ % right). UTS (magenta squares), YS (blue diamonds), TE (black triangles) and δ (red crosses at ~10 and 12 wt% Al). Solid = water quenched, dotted = quenched + aged 550 °C/24 h. Solid UTS shows a low-Al minimum then a rise; dotted UTS rises steeply above ~8 wt% Al.

Tensile properties of Fe-30Mn-0.4C-xAl versus Al (wt%) from 0 to 11, same dual-axis layout and symbol scheme. UTS and YS both dip to a minimum near 2 wt% Al then rise steeply; TE peaks at 2 wt% Al and decreases at higher Al while δ increases monotonically from near zero to roughly 60%. Dotted (aged) and solid (quenched) curves nearly overlap.

Tensile properties of Fe-30Mn-9Al-xC versus C (wt%) from 0 to 2, left axis extended to 1200 MPa. UTS increases from ~800 MPa to above 1000 MPa and YS from ~450 MPa to near 900 MPa with increasing C; TE peaks near 0.75 wt% C and then declines; δ (red crosses) drops steeply from about 50% at 0.3 wt% C to near zero at 1 wt% C. This panel is not described in the supplied caption.

unreadable_items: error bars on several UTS/YS data points in panels (a) and (b) are too small at the supplied resolution to quantify
caption text describing the figure begins with a stray duplicate '(a) (b)' heading and provides no description of panel (c)
exact numerical values of the plotted data points are not printed on any panel and cannot be read from the axes
